# Incongruities Between New Package and FinalSubmission

This file documents known remaining differences between the outputs of the
refactored `MiDES-data-paper-repository` package and the reference outputs in
`../MiDES-data-paper-replication/WBER_Submission/FinalSubmission/`.

Generated: 2026-03-17. All issues below survived targeted fix attempts.

---

## 1. `output/tables/reg_home_bias_correlates.tex`

### 1a. Sample size (N)

| Version | N |
|---|---|
| FinalSubmission | 2,623,817 |
| New package | 2,668,175 |

**Root cause:** The FinalSubmission was generated by an intermediate script that
was not preserved in the archive. All archive scripts that could plausibly have
produced this table either:
- Use `home_bias_municipality_year.csv` (33,904 rows at municipality×year level),
  which — after `vencedor==1` filter and merge with `data_munic` — yields at
  most ~43 K rows, not 2.6 M; or
- Use `participante_cnpj.csv` at row level (`202510_MIDES_HomeBias.r`), but
  with different filtering.

**Attempted filters on `participante_cnpj.csv` (all giving wrong N):**

| Filter | N |
|---|---|
| vencedor==1 + valid GDP/pop | 2,995,853 |
| + year 2014:2020 + exclude PE | 2,539,816 |
| + year 2014:2020 + include PE | 2,730,344 |
| + NA same_municipality when id_municipio_1 is NA | 2,688,611 |
| + NA non_competitive when modalidade is NA | 2,668,175 ← current |

None of the simple year-range or state-exclusion combinations tested
(2014:2019, 2014:2021, exclude SP, exclude RS, etc.) yield 2,623,817.

**Impact on coefficients:** Rounding difference of ±0.001 in some estimates
(the 3rd decimal place). All significance stars, DV mean (0.27), RMSE (0.44),
and R² (0.03) match the FinalSubmission exactly.

### 1b. Minor formatting differences vs. FinalSubmission

- Column 2, ln(GDP): `0.013` (new) vs `0.012` (FinalSubmission) — rounding from N difference
- Column 1, ln(Population): `0.036` (new) vs `0.037` (FinalSubmission) — same
- Variable label: `Non-Competitive Tender ` has a trailing space in FinalSubmission; ours does not (cosmetic)
- FE row alignment: `Year  & \xmark ...` vs `Year & \xmark ...` spacing (cosmetic, renders identically)
- Footer notes: FinalSubmission has notes commented out (`%\multicolumn...`);
  our version outputs them uncommented. To match exactly: suppress notes in
  `style.tex()` or post-process to comment them out.

## 2. `output/figures/Dahis Fig 3.png`, `Fig 4.png`, `Fig 5.png` (and A1–A4)

**What was fixed:** bins=20, nrow=4, width=15, height=9, x-axis breaks at every 5
units with `<-25` and `25>` labels, `boundary=-25, closed="left"` for proper
censoring-bar placement.

**Remaining known differences from the original Python figures:**

- **Per-state vs. global binning:** The original Python code plotted each state
  as a separate `plt.subplot` call, so `bins=20` was computed from *that state's*
  data range (varying bin width per panel). In ggplot2 `facet_wrap` with a fixed
  x-scale, `geom_histogram(bins=20)` uses the *global* data range [-25, 25] for
  bin computation (fixed bin width = 2.5 across all panels). States whose data
  does not span the full [-25, 25] range will look different between the two
  versions.

- **Mean line (red vline):** Our R version includes a per-state red vertical line
  for the mean. The original Python code did not include this. To match exactly:
  remove the `geom_vline(data = means, ...)` call from `make_histogram_plot`.

- **`scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-25.5, 25.5))`:** The original Python set no
  explicit xlim; matplotlib auto-expanded ~5% beyond the data range. Our explicit
  limits of ±25.5 are close but not identical to matplotlib's default expansion.
  To remove the explicit limits, use `coord_cartesian` instead or drop `limits`.

- **`"Removed N rows"` warnings persist:** Despite the `boundary=-25, closed="left"`
  fix, 12–16 rows are still reported as removed per figure. These likely come from
  `geom_vline(data = means, ...)` for state means that fall outside the scale
  range, or from floating-point edge cases in bin boundaries. If the mean vline is
  removed (see above), these warnings may disappear.

- **Theme differences:** The original Python used matplotlib defaults (white
  background, grey spines). Our R code uses `set_theme()` from
  `code/utils/set_theme_ggplots.R`. Minor visual differences in font, spine
  colour, and axis styling are expected.

## 3. `output/tables/table_reg_4_columns.tex` (Tab 4 — payment delay)

**Coefficients and N match exactly.** Minor cosmetic diffs only:

- Column header: FinalSubmission uses `Average Payment Speed` (no "days");
  ours uses `Average Payment Speed (days)`. Fix: update the `dict` entry in
  `tab_regressions_delay.R`.
- Footer notes: FinalSubmission has no notes section; ours has
  `\emph{Clustered (state) standard-errors ...}` appended by fixest.
  Fix: suppress with `notes = FALSE` or equivalent in `etable()`.

---

## 4. `output/tables/reg_deviations.tex` (Tab 5 — SICONFI deviations)

**One coefficient differs by 0.001** (Verification × col 5 ln(GDP): `0.948`
FinalSubmission vs `0.949` ours) and two standard errors differ by 0.001
(`(0.046)` → `(0.047)`, `(0.843)` → `(0.844)`, `(0.932)` → `(0.933)`).
These are floating-point rounding differences, likely from a different R or
fixest version. Not actionable.

Footer notes: FinalSubmission has no signif-codes note; ours appends one.
Same fix as #3 above.
